findings.issue_text: Grant type context (Constants.GRANT_TYPE) is set only in exchangeClientToOIDCClient; the other primary token-exchange paths that mint tokens via tokenManager.responseBuilder().generateAccessToken() → initToken — exchangeOIDCToOIDCClient (the most common RFC 8693 flow), KcOidcBrokerTokenExchangeProvider, KcSamlBrokerTokenExchangeProvider, and external→internal brokering exchanges — never set it, so their tokens silently fall back to the UNKNOWN "na" sentinel and the TokenExchangeGrantTypeFactory "te" shortcut is unreachable in practice (StandardTokenExchangeProvider.java:237)

In AccessTokenContext.java:76-79, the null check for rawTokenId is a copy-paste bug that re-checks grantType (Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")), so a null raw id is silently accepted and encodeTokenId emits a jti ending in ":null" that gets persisted to events and issued to clients instead of failing fast at construction
AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId has an inverted condition: it returns false (no match) exactly when the grant shortcut equals the expected value — the comparison must be negated with !

AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId has an off-by-one slice: it uses substring(3, 5) instead of the documented substring(4, 6), grabbing the last char of the token type plus the first char of the grant, so the condition can never fire and grant assertions degenerate to "anything shaped X:uuid passes"; additionally any prefix shorter than 5 chars throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException (a test error, not a clean failure)

OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut() javadoc promises "usually like 3-letters shortcut", but the default decoder hard-requires a fixed 2+2+2 layout (encodedContext.length() != 6 → IllegalArgumentException) and encodeTokenId performs no length validation, so a custom grant factory following the documented contract can issue tokens that hard-fail at decode time
Removed public Context(Context) copy constructor in OAuth2GrantType breaks binary compatibility — code compiled against it hits NoSuchMethodError at runtime

New mandatory abstract method getShortcut() on OAuth2GrantTypeFactory breaks existing third-party implementations — provider load fails at boot (AbstractMethodError/instantiation failure), bricking deployments using custom grants

grantsByShortcuts.put(grantShortcut, ...) is a ConcurrentHashMap.put in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit, so a factory returning a null shortcut or id throws a bare NPE — a deployment-wide startup crash with no indication of which provider caused it, unlike the descriptive IllegalStateException added for duplicate-shortcut detection

OAuth2GrantType.Context constructor now dereferences formParams (this.grantType = formParams.getFirst(...)), so any code constructing a Context with null form params and populating later via setFormParams — the previously-supported deferred pattern used by CIBA-style grants — NPEs immediately at request time

grantType is frozen at Context construction and setFormParams does not resync it, so a grant that builds its Context from replacement form params loses its grant type entirely and falls back to "na" in encoding — an implicit, undocumented ordering assumption

testIncorrectGrantType passes via a NullPointerException instead of the intended validation branch: the test never calls postInit so DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.sessionFactory is null, the lazy-refresh branch NPEs on unknown shortcut "ac", and the over-broad catch (RuntimeException) swallows the difference — the IllegalArgumentException("Unknown value 'ac'...") path has zero coverage

Access-token jti and Details.TOKEN_ID format changes from UUID to "<ctx>:<uuid>" (TokenManager.initToken ~line 1051) — a wire-visible format change that can break consumers treating jti as a UUID-shaped opaque value (event/audit pipelines with UUID constraints, tests not using updated AssertEvents helpers, DB column validators), and the same logical token has a different shape pre/post upgrade

Adding the new abstract getShortcut() method to the OAuth2GrantTypeFactory interface (OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.java:31) is a binary-incompatible SPI change: third-party grant factories compiled against the previous interface throw AbstractMethodError at startup when DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit (lines 69-76) unconditionally calls gtf.getShortcut() on every registered factory, crashing Keycloak boot for any deployment with a custom grant extension

DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit does not guard against a factory's getShortcut() returning null: grantsByShortcuts.put(null, grantName) throws a NullPointerException (ConcurrentHashMap rejects null keys), an obscure startup crash with no diagnostic, unlike the intentional IllegalStateException used for duplicate shortcuts
Removing the public Context(Context) copy constructor from OAuth2GrantType is a binary-incompatible change that breaks existing callers with NoSuchMethodError

encodeTokenId (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:99-112) throws IllegalStateException on any grant type with no registered provider, causing a 500 on token issuance whenever the GRANT_TYPE client-session attribute holds an unregistered value; this is reachable when a grant provider (including third-party) internally serves grant_type values different from its registered ID, since OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse stamps the raw form value

getTokenContextFromTokenId (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:73-74, 82-91) throws IllegalArgumentException on any colon-containing, non-conformant token ID, so tokens issued under a grant provider that is later disabled or undeployed (e.g., feature-flag flips for pc/pre-authorized_code, CIBA, or a removed extension) become undecodable even though they are signature-valid

Unknown 2-char shortcuts trigger a full getProviderFactoriesStream scan on every call with no negative caching, so repeated malformed or foreign token IDs cause repeated scans, a DoS-shaped availability hazard given this provider is the intended hook for future request-path token inspection

Grant-type stamping is incomplete: only the exchangeClientToOIDCClient path in StandardTokenExchangeProvider (line 237) sets Constants.GRANT_TYPE; external-to-internal token exchange and any custom grant that does not route through OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse leave the attribute unset, so their tokens encode as 'na', making the decoded grant-type field ambiguous and untrustworthy for downstream consumers

PreAuthorizedCodeGrantType (line 82) sets the GRANT_TYPE attribute on a locally constructed DefaultClientSessionContext, which may not be the context that survives to initToken, so the stamping may be lost

Duplicate-shortcut validation (grantsByShortcuts.size() != grantsToShortcuts.size()) only runs once in postInit (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:81-83); the lazy refresh paths (lines 106-125) put into both maps without collision detection, so two hot-deployed grants sharing a shortcut silently overwrite each other (last-write-wins in grantsByShortcuts), causing decoding to misattribute the grant type with no error

AccessTokenContext's rawTokenId null guard is a copy-paste of the grantType check: Objects.requireNonNull is called on grantType twice (the second time with the message 'Null rawTokenId not allowed'), so rawTokenId is never actually null-checked and a null would be string-concatenated into jti as the literal 'null' in encodeTokenId instead of failing fast

The new isAccessTokenId test matcher in AssertEvents (around lines 476-491) has an inverted predicate: 'if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;' returns no-match precisely when the grant shortcut equals the expected value

The isAccessTokenId matcher also reads the wrong indices: it reads substring(3, 5) (indices 3-4) but the grant shortcut occupies indices 4-5 of the 6-char prefix (session=0-1, token type=2-3, grant=4-5); the wrong indices mask the inversion, so the matcher accepts any well-formed prefixed ID with a UUID tail regardless of grant type, making all four updated Details.TOKEN_ID assertions (code-to-token, device, refresh, CIBA) vacuous about the grant type and allowing a future regression that swaps grant shortcuts to pass CI

DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.getShortcutByGrantType/getGrantTypeByShortcut (~lines 98-127) re-stream all OAuth2GrantType factories on every cache miss and never memoize the negative result, so unknown values trigger a repeated full scan (which then throws) on every subsequent call; the 'refresh maps in case a new grant type was deployed' branch is effectively dead in steady state since provider factories aren't hot-deployed, and only fires during version skew/rolling upgrades or undeployed custom grants where every token decode/validation request pays the rescan before failing — the registry should be resolved once at startup (treating unknowns as plain failures) or negatives should be cached

AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId matcher (AssertEvents.java ~477-486) has an inverted comparison: `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` rejects *matching* IDs, so the condition can never be true for real token IDs and the matcher accepts any grant shortcut

AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId matcher uses the wrong substring index: the grant shortcut occupies chars 4-5 of the token ID, so the slice should be substring(4, 6), not substring(3, 5), which reads the last char of tokenType plus the first char of grantType

The vacuous grant-shortcut assertion in AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId means expectCodeToToken, expectRefresh, expectDeviceCodeToToken, and expectAuthReqIdToToken assert nothing about the grant encoding (the headline behavior of the PR), so a regression emitting the wrong shortcut would not be caught, giving false confidence; fix: `return items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut) && isUUID().matches(items[1]);`

AccessTokenContext.java:69-70 constructor runs `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null grantType not allowed")` twice due to a copy-paste error; the second check was meant to be `requireNonNull(rawTokenId, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")`, so the non-null invariant on rawTokenId is not enforced — latent, but a future null caller would surface as a malformed "...:null" token ID or an NPE far from the real cause

DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit (~line 72) calls `grantsByShortcuts.put(grantShortcut, grantName)` without a null check; a custom OAuth2GrantTypeFactory whose newly added (and undocumented-as-non-null) getShortcut() returns null causes a ConcurrentHashMap NPE that crashes server startup with no pointer to the offending provider — the duplicate-shortcut guard only covers duplicates, not nulls; a null/blank check throwing a descriptive IllegalStateException naming the factory would fail fast and diagnosably

Unconditional change to every access token's `jti` format from a plain UUID to `<shortcut>:<uuid>` (e.g. `onrtac:...`) in `TokenManager.initToken` / `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId`, with no feature flag, realm/client opt-in, or version marker — breaks external consumers that parse/validate `jti` as a UUID (audit/SIEM pipelines, DB schemas with UUID-typed columns), changes the `Details.TOKEN_ID` value in login events consumed via the Admin Events API, and mixed fleets during rolling upgrades will emit both formats with no migration surface

New abstract `getShortcut()` method added to the public SPI `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` breaks existing custom-grant extensions: old factories won't recompile, and at runtime `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit` calls `gtf.getShortcut()` on every registered grant factory during `KeycloakSessionFactory` deployment, so a legacy-compiled custom grant throws `AbstractMethodError` and aborts the entire server startup instead of degrading; a `default` method (derive from `getId()` or return the `UNKNOWN` shortcut) would have preserved source and binary compatibility

`isAccessTokenId` matcher in `AssertEvents` slices the wrong characters for the grant shortcut: it uses `substring(3, 5)` (tokenType[1] + grantType[0]) instead of `substring(4, 6)` per the encoded layout `[0-2]=sessionType, [2-4]=tokenType, [4-6]=grantType`

`isAccessTokenId` matcher inverts the grant-shortcut check — `if (…equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` rejects on match — so `expectCodeToToken`/`expectRefresh`/`expectDeviceCodeToToken`/`expectAuthReqIdToToken` pass for any token whose UUID part is a UUID regardless of grant shortcut (e.g. `expectRefresh` happily accepts `onrtac:<uuid>`), making the feature's only test guardrail vacuous and letting future encoding regressions sail through
Public `OAuth2GrantType.Context(Context)` copy constructor deleted outright — binary break for any extension calling it, with no deprecation cycle

The surviving `OAuth2GrantType.Context` constructor now executes `this.grantType = formParams.getFirst(OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE)`, so a caller passing null formParams (previously legal, since a `setFormParams` mutator exists for deferred population) gets an immediate NPE

`OAuth2GrantType.Context.setFormParams` still exists but no longer updates `grantType`, so a caller that constructs with placeholder params and replaces them later will bake the wrong grant type into the token's encoded `jti` via `createTokenResponse` -> `context.getGrantType()`

`getShortcut()` javadoc says the shortcut is 'usually like 3-letters' while all built-ins are 2 chars, and nothing validates a factory's shortcut length/format at registration, yet the decoder `getTokenContextFromTokenId` requires exactly a 6-char prefix and hard-fails with `IllegalArgumentException: Expected length of 6` — a third-party grant following the javadoc produces token IDs that are permanently un-decodable

Inconsistent decoder strictness: legacy colon-less IDs degrade gracefully to `UNKNOWN`, but a well-formed 6-char prefix with an unknown value throws; since the new wire format has no version marker and token IDs are ultimately client-supplied input, the strict-throw decode path is a compat time bomb for previously issued tokens once decoding is wired into runtime flows

Lazy refresh paths in `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory` (`getShortcutByGrantType` / `getGrantTypeByShortcut`) insert into the shared `ConcurrentHashMap`s with no collision check, bypassing the `postInit` duplicate validation — a custom grant whose shortcut collides with a built-in (e.g. `cc`) silently overwrites `grantsByShortcuts[cc]`, so `client_credentials` tokens still encode `cc` but decode to the custom grant, breaking the round-trip with no error
A grant factory whose `getShortcut()` returns null causes an NPE from `ConcurrentHashMap.put(null, ...)` during `postInit`, failing server boot with an unrelated-looking error

The `postInit` duplicate-shortcut check throws `IllegalStateException`, aborting the entire server startup over an extension's shortcut choice — it should arguably warn or disable the offending grant instead of aborting boot

`AccessTokenContext` constructor null-checks `grantType` twice — `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, 'Null grantType not allowed')` followed by `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, 'Null rawTokenId not allowed')` — the second check should target `rawTokenId`; as written a null `rawTokenId` is accepted and `encodeTokenId` will emit `prefix:null`, which then decodes to the literal string `null`

Token-exchange paths other than `exchangeClientToOIDCClient` (e.g. `exchangeExternalToken` external-token import) never set the `GRANT_TYPE` attribute, and `TokenExchangeGrantType.process` bypasses `OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse` so the attribute is only set where manually added — their access tokens encode `UNKNOWN` (`na`) instead of `te`; the diff patches exactly one of several token-producing methods in `StandardTokenExchangeProvider` and the added `TokenExchangeGrantTypeFactory` import is left unused, indicating incomplete coverage

New SPI method `getShortcut()` added to `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` without a `default` implementation: pre-compiled third-party grant factories lack the method and fail lazily with `AbstractMethodError` inside `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit()`, aborting `DefaultKeycloakSessionFactory` initialization so the entire Keycloak instance refuses to boot after upgrade for deployments with custom grant extensions
The PR deletes the public `Context(Context)` copy constructor in `OAuth2GrantType.java`, breaking pre-compiled callers with `NoSuchMethodError`

Shortcut format is never validated (no length, charset, or ':' checks) at registration time (`postInit` checks only uniqueness) or at `encodeTokenId`, while the decoder hard-requires the context part to be exactly 6 chars (2+2+2) and the extension-point Javadoc tells implementers a 3-letter shortcut is usual — a third-party grant following the documented contract boots and encodes fine but every token ID is permanently rejected by `getTokenContextFromTokenId` with `IllegalArgumentException` (fail-late trap)

`AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId` matcher is doubly broken with two canceling bugs — an off-by-one extraction (`substring(3, 5)` instead of `substring(4, 6)`) and an inverted condition (returns false when the grant equals the expected value) — so it accepts any `"<prefix>:<uuid>"` regardless of grant type, making the new grant-encoding verification in `expectCodeToToken`, `expectRefresh`, `expectDeviceCodeToToken`, and `expectAuthReqIdToToken` vacuous; fixing either bug alone flips all four tests to failing
`substring(3, 5)` in `AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId` throws `StringIndexOutOfBoundsException` rather than returning false for prefixes shorter than 5 chars

`AccessTokenContext` constructor null-checks the wrong field: `grantType` is checked twice (copy-paste duplicate with the misleading message "Null rawTokenId not allowed") while `rawTokenId` is never checked, so a null `rawTokenId` silently passes and later encodes as the literal "...:null" in the token ID instead of failing fast at the boundary

Lazy grant-map refresh in `getShortcutByGrantType`/`getGrantTypeByShortcut` (`DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory`) bypasses the startup uniqueness invariant: a late-registered grant whose shortcut collides with an existing one silently overwrites the shortcut→grant mapping while `grantsToShortcuts` keeps both grants, causing silent encode/decode divergence with no error logged and no fail-fast

`testIncorrectGrantType` passes via an unintended NPE: `before()` calls `init(null)` without ever calling `postInit`, so `sessionFactory` stays null and the refresh path dereferences it → `NullPointerException` swallowed by the blanket `catch (RuntimeException)`; the intended `IllegalArgumentException("Unknown value ... for grant type")` branch is never executed, leaving the unknown-grant-shortcut validation path with zero real coverage

Grant type is tagged only in `exchangeClientToOIDCClient`: the user-subject token exchange path in `StandardTokenExchangeProvider` issues access tokens via the same `responseBuilder().generateAccessToken()` without setting the `Constants.GRANT_TYPE` attribute, so the most common token-exchange path encodes grant context as "na" (UNKNOWN), inconsistent with "te" on the sibling path and undetectable by CI since the only verifying matcher is broken

Asymmetric error handling in `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider`: a null grant type degrades gracefully to UNKNOWN/"na" (`:56-60`) but a non-null unregistered grant type throws `IllegalStateException` from `encodeTokenId` via `TokenManager.initToken`, hard-failing the entire token request with HTTP 500 — a fail-closed optional metadata-enrichment step on a free-form, publicly settable client-session attribute, an extension-triggered outage path

AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId (testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/AssertEvents.java:476-488) has an inverted comparison: `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` returns "no match" when the grant shortcut equals the expected value.

AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId uses an off-by-one slice: per encodeTokenId the encoded context is sessionType(2) + tokenType(2) + grant(2), so the grant shortcut is at substring(4, 6), not substring(3, 5). The two bugs cancel out — substring(3,5) grabs fragments that never equal any expected grant shortcut — so the matcher always falls through to the UUID check and expectCodeToToken, expectDeviceCodeToToken, expectRefresh, and expectAuthReqIdToToken assert nothing about the encoded grant type; a token minted with the wrong grant (or no encoding beyond a colon) passes, and fixing only the index later would make every one of these tests fail.
No length guard before substring(3, 5) in AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId, so a short prefix causes a StringIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of a clean mismatch.

The global change of token IDs from UUID to 'onrtac:<uuid>'-style strings for every issued jti (TokenManager.initToken, services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/TokenManager.java:1048-1055) has no end-to-end assertion: no test verifies the actual AccessToken.getId()/jti shape from a real flow per grant type (auth code → 'ac', refresh → 'rt', client-credentials transient → 'tr', offline refresh → 'of', exchange → 'te', device → 'dg', ciba → 'ci'); only 4 event expectations were updated, and token exchange, password, UMA, and client-credentials flows have no assertions on their encoded token IDs, so regressions in this de-facto contract consumed by event logs and downstream parsers are invisible to CI.
sessionType and tokenType prefixes are never asserted anywhere — nothing verifies transient sessions encode 'tr', lightweight tokens encode 'lt', or offline refresh encodes 'of'.

DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest.testIncorrectGrantType (~79-87) passes for the wrong reason: postInit is never called so factory.sessionFactory is null, and decoding 'ofrtac:5678' reaches getGrantTypeByShortcut('ac') → map miss → sessionFactory.getProviderFactoriesStream(...) → NPE, which is swallowed by the overly broad catch (RuntimeException); the intended IllegalArgumentException("Unknown value … for grant type") branch in getTokenContextFromTokenId is never executed, so the test would pass even if the IAE logic were deleted and the lazy-refresh path (real production code for hot-deployed grants) is never exercised — it should catch IllegalArgumentException and assert the message.

DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest.before() (~37-50) hand-seeds grantsByShortcuts/grantsToShortcuts directly with 3 hand-picked entries instead of exercising DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit, leaving real map construction from actual OAuth2GrantTypeFactory providers, the duplicate-ID/shortcut validation (IllegalStateException on size mismatch), the UNKNOWN sentinel seeding, and both lazy re-lookup branches with zero coverage; the duplicate-shortcut guardrail for the 'shortcut should be unique across grants' contract is never verified to fire.

Production entry point DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext (~46-68), invoked by TokenManager.initToken for every access-token issuance, is completely untested: TRANSIENT vs isOffline() vs ONLINE resolution, getShouldUseLightweightToken integration, and the grantType == null → 'na' fallback have no coverage (unit tests only decode/encode synthetic strings), so a regression here (e.g., NPE on an unexpected session state, or offline sessions encoded as ONLINE) is caught by nothing.

Copy-paste null-check bug in AccessTokenContext (~66-69): Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed") null-checks grantType twice while rawTokenId is effectively unchecked, so a null rawTokenId would silently produce 'onrtac:null' token IDs in any future caller deviating from KeycloakModelUtils.generateId(); no unit test constructs AccessTokenContext with null arguments, which would have exposed this immediately.

Missing decoder edge-case tests for the IllegalArgumentException branches of getTokenContextFromTokenId (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider ~70-104): encoded-context length ≠ 6 (e.g., 'onrta:1234' or 'onrtacc:1234'), unknown session-type shortcut (e.g., 'xxrtac:1'), unknown token-type shortcut (e.g., 'onxxac:1'), and raw ID containing a colon (indexOf takes the first colon while isAccessTokenId's split(":") assumes exactly one) are untested, leaving the API-facing error semantics unpinned.

Constants.GRANT_TYPE is set only in exchangeClientToOIDCClient (services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/tokenexchange/StandardTokenExchangeProvider.java:237); any other exchange path that mints an access token via responseBuilder without going through OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse will silently encode 'na', and there is no test asserting what a token-exchanged access token's ID encodes ('te' vs 'na'), so the expected encoding per exchange path is unpinned and can drift.

AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId grant-shortcut check is dead logic: the condition is inverted (returns false exactly when the grant shortcut is correct) and the substring window is off by one (substring(3, 5) instead of substring(4, 6), given the encoded prefix is sessionType(2)+tokenType(2)+grantType(2)), making the equality branch unreachable - the matcher never verifies the grant type, so all four call sites (expectCodeToToken, expectDeviceCodeToToken, expectRefresh, expectAuthReqIdToToken) pass vacuously, producing false green CI for the PR's central feature; fixing only one of the two bugs would make correct tokens fail the assertions
items[0].substring(3, 5) in AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException (escaping matchesSafely) for any encoded prefix shorter than 5 characters

getShortcut() was added as a non-default abstract method on OAuth2GrantTypeFactory, breaking all existing custom grant implementations - deployed custom factories that are not recompiled will fail provider instantiation at startup and their grant stops working after upgrade; a default method returning a safe value (e.g. the id or "na") would preserve compatibility

Hidden invariant: the decoder hard-requires exactly 2-char shortcuts (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider's encodedContext.length() != 6 check), but the getShortcut() javadoc misleadingly suggests a '3-letters' shortcut and factory postInit validates uniqueness but never length - a custom grant returning a 1- or 3-char shortcut will encode fine but the framework throws IllegalArgumentException when decoding; the length contract must be documented on the interface and enforced at startup

Grant-type state is set in five scattered locations (OAuth2GrantTypeBase.java:109, ResourceOwnerPasswordCredentialsGrantType.java:134, PreAuthorizedCodeGrantType.java:82, StandardTokenExchangeProvider.java:237, and TokenManager.java:248's hardcoded OAuth2Constants.REFRESH_TOKEN) with no choke point - forgetting to set Constants.GRANT_TYPE fails silently (token encodes as "na" with no warning), while a typo'd or unregistered value makes encodeTokenId throw IllegalStateException and turns the token endpoint into a 500

Duplicate-shortcut validation for the grants SPI lives inside the encoder factory's postInit (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory) - an invariant of OAuth2GrantTypeFactory is enforced by a different SPI's provider factory, so replacing the default encoder provider silently removes validation

The lazy-refresh paths in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory (getShortcutByGrantType/getGrantTypeByShortcut, lines ~104-138) insert into the maps without re-running the collision check, so a refresh-time collision silently overwrites grantsByShortcuts and the shortcut decodes to the wrong grant for previously issued tokens; the refresh paths are also speculative complexity since Keycloak does not hot-deploy providers into a running KeycloakSessionFactory

AccessTokenContext constructor copy-paste bug: the fourth null check re-checks grantType instead of rawTokenId (Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")), so a null rawTokenId passes validation and would later stringify as "onrtcc:null" in the token ID instead of failing fast

The entire decode path (getTokenContextFromTokenId, its exception types, the UNKNOWN legacy fallback, and the factory refresh logic) has zero production callers and is exercised only by unit tests - speculative API surface that freezes the format contract and decode error semantics into a public SPI before anything consumes them

Redundant grant-type attribute writes: ResourceOwnerPasswordCredentialsGrantType.java:134's explicit setAttribute(Constants.GRANT_TYPE, ...) is immediately overwritten with the identical value by the inherited createTokenResponse in OAuth2GrantTypeBase.java:109 (same likely applies to PreAuthorizedCodeGrantType.java:82) - harmless today but seeds confusion about which write is authoritative and invites divergence

Layering leak: the encode package now depends on protocol.oidc.mappers, and AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.getShouldUseLightweightToken was widened to public static solely so the encoder can call it - lightweight-token policy belongs in a neutral OIDC config utility, and the new mappers-encode dependency widens API surface and will make future refactoring awkward

Constants.GRANT_TYPE is a pure alias of OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE - two public constants with the same name and value in sibling classes is a standing invitation to use the wrong one and creates future divergence confusion; referencing OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE at the use sites would suffice

OAuth2GrantType.Context.grantType snapshots unvalidated client input at construction time (formParams.getFirst(OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE)) instead of deriving it from the provider's own factory ID - it can be null if form params lack the key and goes stale if the public setFormParams is later used to swap parameters; the authoritative value should be the factory ID the endpoint dispatched on

Unit test passes for the wrong reason: DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest's before() calls init(null) but never postInit so sessionFactory is null, and in testIncorrectGrantType the refresh path throws an NPE that is swallowed by the broad catch (RuntimeException) - the test never exercises the IllegalArgumentException branch it claims to verify; the test also seeds package-private mutable factory fields (factory.grantsByShortcuts) directly, coupling it to factory internals

Likely-unused import TokenExchangeGrantTypeFactory added in StandardTokenExchangeProvider.java:50 - the added line uses OAuth2Constants.TOKEN_EXCHANGE_GRANT_TYPE directly and there is no GRANT_TYPE constant on that factory; leftover from an abandoned approach

Public OAuth2GrantType.Context(Context) copy constructor was removed - external grant implementations that construct derived contexts this way will no longer compile; a deprecated forwarding constructor would have been safer if removal was necessary

The token-ID wire format is a persisted, cross-version contract but is implemented as a swappable per-deployment SPI (TokenContextEncoderSpi) with no feature flag, migration note, or documentation that the format must remain stable - swapping the TokenContextEncoderProvider orphans every previously issued token ID and a custom provider has no stated compatibility obligation; the format should be treated as a versioned contract

AssertEvents.java:483 (isAccessTokenId matcher): inverted logic — the matcher returns false (mismatch) when the grant shortcut equals the expected value and falls through to pass when it doesn't, so a correct token would fail the assertion while a wrong-grant token passes as long as the tail is a UUID

AssertEvents.java:483 (isAccessTokenId matcher): wrong substring index — the grant shortcut occupies chars 4–5 so substring(4, 6) is required, not substring(3, 5), which reads the last char of the token type plus the first char of the grant type (e.g. 'ta' for 'onrtac') and throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException on short prefixes; fixing only the inversion without the index would make every legitimate token fail, and combined the guard can never reject anything, so the four updated assertions (expectCodeToToken, expectDeviceCodeToToken, expectRefresh, expectAuthReqIdToToken) verify nothing about grant encoding and the PR's only end-to-end integration check goes green even if the encoding is entirely wrong

DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:74 (decoder) vs :110–118 (encoder) and OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.java:29–33 (contract): the decoder hard-requires the context prefix to be exactly 6 chars (i.e. 2-char shortcuts) while the encoder blindly concatenates getShortcut() output with no length check and postInit performs no format validation, and the getShortcut() javadoc explicitly invites 3-letter shortcuts — a custom grant returning e.g. 'abc' mints tokens that encodeTokenId accepts but whose getTokenContextFromTokenId always throws IllegalArgumentException (mint path green, decode path red, no startup-time detection)

DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:76: a grant factory whose getShortcut() returns null NPEs in ConcurrentHashMap.put during postInit, causing whole-server boot failure with a confusing NPE because there is no null check on shortcuts
A grant shortcut containing ':' silently corrupts the raw-id split in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId

OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.java:31: the new abstract getShortcut() method was added to the factory SPI with no default implementation, so pre-compiled third-party grant extensions (a known custom-grant extension point) throw AbstractMethodError when postInit iterates all factories calling gtf.getShortcut(), preventing the entire Keycloak server from starting after the upgrade
OAuth2GrantType: the public Context(Context) copy constructor was removed, a source break for any extension code using it
OAuth2GrantType: the main Context constructor now calls formParams.getFirst(...) and NPEs on null form params, a pattern the retained setFormParams() mutator implies was previously supported

DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:83–85: the duplicate-check throws during postInit if any two grant factories collide on shortcut or ID (e.g. a third-party grant picking built-in 'ac'), turning a pre-upgrade harmless situation into a whole-server boot failure scoped far beyond the offending provider

adjudication_records.issue_text: grantsByShortcuts.put(grantShortcut, ...) is a ConcurrentHashMap.put in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit, so a factory returning a null shortcut or id throws a bare NPE — a deployment-wide startup crash with no indication of which provider caused it, unlike the descriptive IllegalStateException added for duplicate-shortcut detection

adjudication_records.issue_text: OAuth2GrantType.Context constructor now dereferences formParams (this.grantType = formParams.getFirst(...)), so any code constructing a Context with null form params and populating later via setFormParams — the previously-supported deferred pattern used by CIBA-style grants — NPEs immediately at request time

The finding’s concern about a wire-visible format change that may break consumers expecting UUID-shaped values is therefore grounded in the diff, but it’s not a verifiable “defect” in-code; it’s a compatibility/contract change introduced intentionally by this PR.

However, the diff does not prove this is reachable in core flows (built-in grant factories in the diff all implement `getShortcut()`), so it’s a robustness/extensibility concern rather than a clearly verifiable defect in this PR alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: getTokenContextFromTokenId (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:73-74, 82-91) throws IllegalArgumentException on any colon-containing, non-conformant token ID, so tokens issued under a grant provider that is later disabled or undeployed (e.g., feature-flag flips for pc/pre-authorized_code, CIBA, or a removed extension) become undecodable even though they are signature-valid

Since the factory maps are populated from currently available grant providers in `postInit()` and refreshed only from current providers, a token id created earlier with a shortcut from a grant provider that is later undeployed/disabled would indeed become non-decodable and trigger an exception. However, the diff does not show any call site where this decoding is part of access-token verification/acceptance, so the impact on “signature-valid tokens” being rejected can’t be verified from the PR alone; it’s a legitimate robustness/compatibility concern introduced by the strict decoding behavior, but not a proven broken behavior in this diff by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unknown 2-char shortcuts trigger a full getProviderFactoriesStream scan on every call with no negative caching, so repeated malformed or foreign token IDs cause repeated scans, a DoS-shaped availability hazard given this provider is the intended hook for future request-path token inspection

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory#getGrantTypeByShortcut, if a 2-char shortcut is not found in grantsByShortcuts, the code performs sessionFactory.getProviderFactoriesStream(OAuth2GrantType.class) to try to discover a matching factory, but if none exists it does not record any negative result. Therefore repeated calls with the same unknown shortcut will repeat the full stream scan each time. This is a diff-grounded performance/availability concern (potentially exploitable if this decoding is on a hot/request path), but the diff does not show that getTokenContextFromTokenId/getGrantTypeByShortcut is currently invoked on attacker-controlled request paths, so it’s not a verifiable concrete defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Duplicate-shortcut validation (grantsByShortcuts.size() != grantsToShortcuts.size()) only runs once in postInit (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:81-83); the lazy refresh paths (lines 106-125) put into both maps without collision detection, so two hot-deployed grants sharing a shortcut silently overwrite each other (last-write-wins in grantsByShortcuts), causing decoding to misattribute the grant type with no error

adjudication_records.issue_text: AccessTokenContext's rawTokenId null guard is a copy-paste of the grantType check: Objects.requireNonNull is called on grantType twice (the second time with the message 'Null rawTokenId not allowed'), so rawTokenId is never actually null-checked and a null would be string-concatenated into jti as the literal 'null' in encodeTokenId instead of failing fast

This is a real logic error in the matcher implementation (and will either reject correct IDs or, combined with the likely-wrong substring range, not validate the grant shortcut as intended).

adjudication_records.issue_text: The isAccessTokenId matcher also reads the wrong indices: it reads substring(3, 5) (indices 3-4) but the grant shortcut occupies indices 4-5 of the 6-char prefix (session=0-1, token type=2-3, grant=4-5); the wrong indices mask the inversion, so the matcher accepts any well-formed prefixed ID with a UUID tail regardless of grant type, making all four updated Details.TOKEN_ID assertions (code-to-token, device, refresh, CIBA) vacuous about the grant type and allowing a future regression that swaps grant shortcuts to pass CI

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.getGrantTypeByShortcut()` does a full `sessionFactory.getProviderFactoriesStream(OAuth2GrantType.class)` scan whenever `grantsByShortcuts.get(shortcut)` is null, and if nothing is found it does not cache that negative result—so the same unknown shortcut will trigger the full scan on every subsequent call before ultimately returning null (and `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId()` will then throw). This is a concrete, diff-grounded performance/behavior concern rather than a functional correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId matcher uses the wrong substring index: the grant shortcut occupies chars 4-5 of the token ID, so the slice should be substring(4, 6), not substring(3, 5), which reads the last char of tokenType plus the first char of grantType

adjudication_records.issue_text: DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit (~line 72) calls `grantsByShortcuts.put(grantShortcut, grantName)` without a null check; a custom OAuth2GrantTypeFactory whose newly added (and undocumented-as-non-null) getShortcut() returns null causes a ConcurrentHashMap NPE that crashes server startup with no pointer to the offending provider — the duplicate-shortcut guard only covers duplicates, not nulls; a null/blank check throwing a descriptive IllegalStateException naming the factory would fail fast and diagnosably

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit(), the diff adds use of the new OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut() and immediately does grantsByShortcuts.put(grantShortcut, grantName) / grantsToShortcuts.put(grantName, grantShortcut) on ConcurrentHashMap without validating grantShortcut. ConcurrentHashMap rejects null keys/values, so any OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementation (including custom providers) returning null for getShortcut() would trigger an NPE during server startup, and the later duplicate-shortcut size check would not catch/null-diagnose it.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unconditional change to every access token's `jti` format from a plain UUID to `<shortcut>:<uuid>` (e.g. `onrtac:...`) in `TokenManager.initToken` / `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId`, with no feature flag, realm/client opt-in, or version marker — breaks external consumers that parse/validate `jti` as a UUID (audit/SIEM pipelines, DB schemas with UUID-typed columns), changes the `Details.TOKEN_ID` value in login events consumed via the Admin Events API, and mixed fleets during rolling upgrades will emit both formats with no migration surface

adjudication.rationale: The diff unconditionally changes the access token ID (`jti`) generation in `TokenManager.initToken` from `KeycloakModelUtils.generateId()` (UUID) to `encoder.encodeTokenId(...)`, and the default encoder formats it as `<6-char context>:<rawTokenId>` (e.g. `onrtac:...`) in `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId`. There is no feature flag/opt-in/version marker shown; the SPI is registered by default (`META-INF/services/...TokenContextEncoderProviderFactory` + `Spi` list). The tests in `AssertEvents` are updated to expect the new `Details.TOKEN_ID` format, confirming the externally visible event payload change. Claims about specific downstream breakages (UUID-typed DB columns, SIEM parsers, mixed rolling-upgrade fleets) are plausible but not directly provable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: New abstract `getShortcut()` method added to the public SPI `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` breaks existing custom-grant extensions: old factories won't recompile, and at runtime `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit` calls `gtf.getShortcut()` on every registered grant factory during `KeycloakSessionFactory` deployment, so a legacy-compiled custom grant throws `AbstractMethodError` and aborts the entire server startup instead of degrading; a `default` method (derive from `getId()` or return the `UNKNOWN` shortcut) would have preserved source and binary compatibility

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new abstract method `String getShortcut()` to the `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` interface (no `default` implementation). This is a binary-incompatible change for any already-compiled `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` implementations (e.g., custom grant factories), which would lack the new method and can throw `AbstractMethodError` when invoked. The new `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit(...)` explicitly iterates all `OAuth2GrantType` provider factories and calls `gtf.getShortcut()` for each during server boot, with no guard/fallback, so such an `AbstractMethodError` would occur during startup and abort initialization rather than degrading gracefully.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `isAccessTokenId` matcher in `AssertEvents` slices the wrong characters for the grant shortcut: it uses `substring(3, 5)` (tokenType[1] + grantType[0]) instead of `substring(4, 6)` per the encoded layout `[0-2]=sessionType, [2-4]=tokenType, [4-6]=grantType`

adjudication.rationale: In `AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId`, the token ID layout encoded by `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId` is 6 chars before `:`: `[0-2)=sessionType` (2 chars), `[2-4)=tokenType` (2 chars), `[4-6)=grantType` (2 chars). The matcher extracts the grant shortcut with `items[0].substring(3, 5)`, which spans the last char of tokenType (index 3) plus the first char of grantType (index 4), instead of `substring(4, 6)`. This is a verifiable off-by-one bug in the diff and will mis-validate access token IDs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `isAccessTokenId` matcher inverts the grant-shortcut check — `if (…equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` rejects on match — so `expectCodeToToken`/`expectRefresh`/`expectDeviceCodeToToken`/`expectAuthReqIdToToken` pass for any token whose UUID part is a UUID regardless of grant shortcut (e.g. `expectRefresh` happily accepts `onrtac:<uuid>`), making the feature's only test guardrail vacuous and letting future encoding regressions sail through

adjudication.rationale: In AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId, matchesSafely rejects when the grant shortcut matches: `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` — the condition is inverted (it should fail when it does *not* equal). Additionally, given the token id format added in this diff (2 chars sessionType + 2 chars tokenType + 2 chars grantShortcut), the grant shortcut would be at substring(4,6), not (3,5). As a result, the updated event expectations (e.g., expectRefresh/expectCodeToToken) no longer correctly validate the grant shortcut and can pass for incorrect encodings.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Public `OAuth2GrantType.Context(Context)` copy constructor deleted outright — binary break for any extension calling it, with no deprecation cycle

adjudication_records.issue_text: `getShortcut()` javadoc says the shortcut is 'usually like 3-letters' while all built-ins are 2 chars, and nothing validates a factory's shortcut length/format at registration, yet the decoder `getTokenContextFromTokenId` requires exactly a 6-char prefix and hard-fails with `IllegalArgumentException: Expected length of 6` — a third-party grant following the javadoc produces token IDs that are permanently un-decodable

adjudication_records.issue_text: Inconsistent decoder strictness: legacy colon-less IDs degrade gracefully to `UNKNOWN`, but a well-formed 6-char prefix with an unknown value throws; since the new wire format has no version marker and token IDs are ultimately client-supplied input, the strict-throw decode path is a compat time bomb for previously issued tokens once decoding is wired into runtime flows

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce the asymmetric decoding behavior: `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId` returns `UNKNOWN` only when there is no `:` (legacy/old format), but for IDs that do have `:` it throws on unexpected prefix length and on unknown shortcuts (`st/tt/gt`) via `IllegalArgumentException`. That concern is grounded in the new decode logic. However, the claim that this is a “compat time bomb for previously issued tokens once decoding is wired into runtime flows” is not verifiable from the diff because decoding is not shown being used in runtime flows here (only encoding is wired into `TokenManager.initToken`). So it’s a real edge-case/robustness/forward-compat design issue, but not a demonstrated defect in current behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Lazy refresh paths in `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory` (`getShortcutByGrantType` / `getGrantTypeByShortcut`) insert into the shared `ConcurrentHashMap`s with no collision check, bypassing the `postInit` duplicate validation — a custom grant whose shortcut collides with a built-in (e.g. `cc`) silently overwrites `grantsByShortcuts[cc]`, so `client_credentials` tokens still encode `cc` but decode to the custom grant, breaking the round-trip with no error

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory` builds `grantsByShortcuts`/`grantsToShortcuts` in `postInit()` and validates duplicates only there via a size comparison. However, both lazy refresh paths explicitly mutate the shared `ConcurrentHashMap`s without any collision/consistency check: `getShortcutByGrantType()` does `grantsByShortcuts.put(shortcut, grantType)` and `grantsToShortcuts.put(grantType, shortcut)`, and `getGrantTypeByShortcut()` similarly does `grantsByShortcuts.put(shortcut, newGrantType)` / `grantsToShortcuts.put(newGrantType, shortcut)`. If a newly discovered/deployed grant returns a shortcut already in use (e.g. "cc"), the `put` overwrites the existing shortcut->grant mapping silently. Because the existing grant->shortcut mapping for the built-in remains, encoding can still emit "cc" for `client_credentials` while decoding "cc" now resolves to the custom grant, breaking round-trip as described.

adjudication_records.issue_text: A grant factory whose `getShortcut()` returns null causes an NPE from `ConcurrentHashMap.put(null, ...)` during `postInit`, failing server boot with an unrelated-looking error

adjudication.rationale: In `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit`, the code unconditionally does `String grantShortcut = gtf.getShortcut(); grantsByShortcuts.put(grantShortcut, grantName);` where `grantsByShortcuts` is a `ConcurrentHashMap` (which forbids null keys/values). If any `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` implementation returns `null` from `getShortcut()`, this will throw an NPE during boot-time `postInit`, matching the finding. The diff introduces `getShortcut()` as a new required method but does not enforce non-null/validate before `put`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The `postInit` duplicate-shortcut check throws `IllegalStateException`, aborting the entire server startup over an extension's shortcut choice — it should arguably warn or disable the offending grant instead of aborting boot

adjudication.rationale: In `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit(...)`, the code builds `grantsByShortcuts` and `grantsToShortcuts` and then enforces uniqueness by throwing an `IllegalStateException` when `grantsByShortcuts.size() != grantsToShortcuts.size()`. This means a duplicate grant shortcut (e.g., from an extension implementing `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory#getShortcut()`) will fail fast and can abort server startup. That behavior is verifiably present in the diff, but whether startup should hard-fail vs. warn/disable is a design/robustness concern rather than a clear correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `AccessTokenContext` constructor null-checks `grantType` twice — `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, 'Null grantType not allowed')` followed by `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, 'Null rawTokenId not allowed')` — the second check should target `rawTokenId`; as written a null `rawTokenId` is accepted and `encodeTokenId` will emit `prefix:null`, which then decodes to the literal string `null`

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `AccessTokenContext` constructor, the fourth null-check mistakenly calls `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` instead of checking `rawTokenId` (see `AccessTokenContext(... String grantType, String rawTokenId)`). This means `rawTokenId` can be null without being rejected. Downstream, `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId(...)` concatenates `':' + tokenContext.getRawTokenId()`, and Java string concatenation will yield the literal `"null"` if `rawTokenId` is null, producing an encoded token id like `prefix:null`, which `getTokenContextFromTokenId` would then parse as raw id `"null"`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Token-exchange paths other than `exchangeClientToOIDCClient` (e.g. `exchangeExternalToken` external-token import) never set the `GRANT_TYPE` attribute, and `TokenExchangeGrantType.process` bypasses `OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse` so the attribute is only set where manually added — their access tokens encode `UNKNOWN` (`na`) instead of `te`; the diff patches exactly one of several token-producing methods in `StandardTokenExchangeProvider` and the added `TokenExchangeGrantTypeFactory` import is left unused, indicating incomplete coverage

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows GRANT_TYPE is set for token exchange only in StandardTokenExchangeProvider.exchangeClientToOIDCClient via `clientSessionCtx.setAttribute(Constants.GRANT_TYPE, OAuth2Constants.TOKEN_EXCHANGE_GRANT_TYPE);`, and the newly added import `org.keycloak.protocol.oidc.grants.TokenExchangeGrantTypeFactory` is indeed unused (suggesting an incomplete/leftover change). However, the claim about other token-exchange paths (e.g., `exchangeExternalToken`) and `TokenExchangeGrantType.process` bypassing `OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse` cannot be verified from the provided diff because those methods/flows are not shown here. adjudication_records.issue_text: New SPI method `getShortcut()` added to `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` without a `default` implementation: pre-compiled third-party grant factories lack the method and fail lazily with `AbstractMethodError` inside `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit()`, aborting `DefaultKeycloakSessionFactory` initialization so the entire Keycloak instance refuses to boot after upgrade for deployments with custom grant extensions

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new abstract method `String getShortcut();` to the `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` interface (no `default` implementation). In `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit()` it iterates `factory.getProviderFactoriesStream(OAuth2GrantType.class)` and unconditionally invokes `gtf.getShortcut()`. Any pre-compiled third-party `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` implementation built against the previous interface would not have this method and would throw `AbstractMethodError` when `postInit()` runs, likely during Keycloak startup, preventing initialization.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The PR deletes the public `Context(Context)` copy constructor in `OAuth2GrantType.java`, breaking pre-compiled callers with `NoSuchMethodError`

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the `public Context(Context context)` copy constructor from `org.keycloak.protocol.oidc.grants.OAuth2GrantType.Context` (server-spi-private). Since it was public, this is a binary-incompatible API change: any precompiled downstream code calling that constructor would hit `NoSuchMethodError` at runtime. The diff alone can’t prove such callers exist, but the compatibility risk is real and directly grounded in the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Shortcut format is never validated (no length, charset, or ':' checks) at registration time (`postInit` checks only uniqueness) or at `encodeTokenId`, while the decoder hard-requires the context part to be exactly 6 chars (2+2+2) and the extension-point Javadoc tells implementers a 3-letter shortcut is usual — a third-party grant following the documented contract boots and encodes fine but every token ID is permanently rejected by `getTokenContextFromTokenId` with `IllegalArgumentException` (fail-late trap)

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces grant-type shortcuts (OAuth2GrantTypeFactory#getShortcut) and encodes them into the access token ID in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider#encodeTokenId by concatenating sessionType(2) + tokenType(2) + grantShort (no length/charset validation) + ':' + rawId. However, DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider#getTokenContextFromTokenId hard-requires the pre-':' context to be exactly 6 chars and then slices the grant shortcut as substring(4,6). DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory#postInit only checks uniqueness via map sizes and never validates that shortcuts are exactly 2 characters and ':'-free. The Javadoc on getShortcut even says “usually like 3-letters shortcut”, which would produce an encoded context length 7 and be permanently rejected by the decoder with IllegalArgumentException. This is a real, diff-grounded correctness trap for third-party grant implementations.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId` matcher is doubly broken with two canceling bugs — an off-by-one extraction (`substring(3, 5)` instead of `substring(4, 6)`) and an inverted condition (returns false when the grant equals the expected value) — so it accepts any `"<prefix>:<uuid>"` regardless of grant type, making the new grant-encoding verification in `expectCodeToToken`, `expectRefresh`, `expectDeviceCodeToToken`, and `expectAuthReqIdToToken` vacuous; fixing either bug alone flips all four tests to failing
`substring(3, 5)` in `AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId` throws `StringIndexOutOfBoundsException` rather than returning false for prefixes shorter than 5 chars

adjudication.rationale: In `AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId`, `matchesSafely` does `items[0].substring(3, 5)` after only checking `items.length == 2`. If the token prefix (`items[0]`) is shorter than 5 characters (e.g., any unexpected value like `"ab:..."`), `substring(3, 5)` will throw `StringIndexOutOfBoundsException` instead of returning `false`, breaking the matcher rather than cleanly failing the assertion. This behavior is directly verifiable from the added code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `AccessTokenContext` constructor null-checks the wrong field: `grantType` is checked twice (copy-paste duplicate with the misleading message "Null rawTokenId not allowed") while `rawTokenId` is never checked, so a null `rawTokenId` silently passes and later encodes as the literal "...:null" in the token ID instead of failing fast at the boundary

adjudication.rationale: In `AccessTokenContext` constructor, the last null-check is `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");` instead of checking `rawTokenId`. This means `rawTokenId` can be null without failing fast, and `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId()` concatenates `':' + tokenContext.getRawTokenId()`, which would yield a token id suffix of `null` rather than throwing at the boundary.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Lazy grant-map refresh in `getShortcutByGrantType`/`getGrantTypeByShortcut` (`DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory`) bypasses the startup uniqueness invariant: a late-registered grant whose shortcut collides with an existing one silently overwrites the shortcut→grant mapping while `grantsToShortcuts` keeps both grants, causing silent encode/decode divergence with no error logged and no fail-fast

adjudication.rationale: In `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory`, uniqueness of grant shortcuts is only validated once in `postInit()` via `if (grantsByShortcuts.size() != grantsToShortcuts.size()) ...`. However, both lazy-refresh paths can later mutate the maps without any collision check: `getShortcutByGrantType()` does `grantsByShortcuts.put(shortcut, grantType)` and `grantsToShortcuts.put(grantType, shortcut)`, which will silently overwrite an existing shortcut→grant mapping if a newly discovered grant reuses a shortcut, while leaving the old grant→shortcut entry intact. This creates encode/decode divergence (encode uses `grantsToShortcuts`, decode uses `grantsByShortcuts`) and no fail-fast/logging occurs. `getGrantTypeByShortcut()` similarly updates both maps on refresh and can overwrite existing mappings.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `testIncorrectGrantType` passes via an unintended NPE: `before()` calls `init(null)` without ever calling `postInit`, so `sessionFactory` stays null and the refresh path dereferences it → `NullPointerException` swallowed by the blanket `catch (RuntimeException)`; the intended `IllegalArgumentException("Unknown value ... for grant type")` branch is never executed, leaving the unknown-grant-shortcut validation path with zero real coverage

adjudication.rationale: In `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest.before()`, the factory is only `init(null)`-ed and the maps are manually populated, but `postInit(...)` is never called, so `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.sessionFactory` remains `null`. In `testIncorrectGrantType`, parsing tokenId `"ofrtac:5678"` leads to `gtShortcut="ac"`, which is not in `grantsByShortcuts`, so `getGrantTypeByShortcut` falls into the refresh path and dereferences `sessionFactory.getProviderFactoriesStream(...)`, causing an NPE. The test then swallows it via `catch (RuntimeException)` and therefore does not actually exercise the intended `IllegalArgumentException("Unknown value ... for grant type")` validation branch in `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Grant type is tagged only in `exchangeClientToOIDCClient`: the user-subject token exchange path in `StandardTokenExchangeProvider` issues access tokens via the same `responseBuilder().generateAccessToken()` without setting the `Constants.GRANT_TYPE` attribute, so the most common token-exchange path encodes grant context as "na" (UNKNOWN), inconsistent with "te" on the sibling path and undetectable by CI since the only verifying matcher is broken

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `clientSessionCtx.setAttribute(Constants.GRANT_TYPE, OAuth2Constants.TOKEN_EXCHANGE_GRANT_TYPE);` being added inside `StandardTokenExchangeProvider.exchangeClientToOIDCClient(...)`, but it does not show the “user-subject token exchange path” code the finding claims is missing the attribute. Since that path is not present in the provided diff hunks, the assertion that the most common token-exchange flow will encode grant type as `na` cannot be verified from this diff alone. (Separately, the new `AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId` matcher does look incorrect: it returns `false` when the expected shortcut matches, but that does not substantiate the specific missing-tag claim.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: Asymmetric error handling in `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider`: a null grant type degrades gracefully to UNKNOWN/"na" (`:56-60`) but a non-null unregistered grant type throws `IllegalStateException` from `encodeTokenId` via `TokenManager.initToken`, hard-failing the entire token request with HTTP 500 — a fail-closed optional metadata-enrichment step on a free-form, publicly settable client-session attribute, an extension-triggered outage path

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext()` treating a missing grant type as non-fatal by mapping `null` to `UNKNOWN` (`na`), but `encodeTokenId()` hard-fails if the grant type is non-null yet not present in `grantsToShortcuts` (`grantShort == null` -> `throw new IllegalStateException(...)`). `TokenManager.initToken()` now always calls `encoder.encodeTokenId(...)`, so an unrecognized value in `clientSessionCtx` under `Constants.GRANT_TYPE` will abort token creation and likely surface as a 500. Since `Constants.GRANT_TYPE` is set from `OAuth2GrantType.Context` using `formParams.getFirst(OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE)`, and also via various flows, the asymmetry (null tolerated, unknown not tolerated) is real and introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId (testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/AssertEvents.java:476-488) has an inverted comparison: `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` returns "no match" when the grant shortcut equals the expected value.

adjudication.rationale: In AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId (new code in the diff), the matcher returns false when the extracted grant shortcut equals the expected value: `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`. That inverts the intended logic (it should fail when NOT equal). As written, it will reject correct token IDs and accept incorrect ones, breaking event assertions. Additionally, given the encoding format elsewhere in the diff (2 chars sessionType + 2 chars tokenType + 2 chars grantType = 6), the grant shortcut should be at substring(4,6), so the indices also appear off-by-one.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId uses an off-by-one slice: per encodeTokenId the encoded context is sessionType(2) + tokenType(2) + grant(2), so the grant shortcut is at substring(4, 6), not substring(3, 5). The two bugs cancel out — substring(3,5) grabs fragments that never equal any expected grant shortcut — so the matcher always falls through to the UUID check and expectCodeToToken, expectDeviceCodeToToken, expectRefresh, and expectAuthReqIdToToken assert nothing about the encoded grant type; a token minted with the wrong grant (or no encoding beyond a colon) passes, and fixing only the index later would make every one of these tests fail.

adjudication.rationale: In AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId, the encoded context format is defined in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider as 6 chars: sessionType(0-2) + tokenType(2-4) + grantType(4-6). The matcher instead inspects items[0].substring(3, 5), which extracts the wrong 2 chars (e.g., for "trltcc" it yields "tc"), so it will not validate the grant shortcut. Additionally, it returns false when the extracted substring equals the expected shortcut, which inverts the intended logic. As written, the matcher effectively only checks that the suffix after ':' is a UUID, so the updated event assertions don’t verify the grant encoding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No length guard before substring(3, 5) in AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId, so a short prefix causes a StringIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of a clean mismatch.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId matcher, after `String[] items = item.split(":");` it only checks `items.length != 2`, but then unconditionally executes `items[0].substring(3, 5)`. If `items[0]` is shorter than 5 characters (e.g., malformed/short token id prefix), this will throw `StringIndexOutOfBoundsException` instead of simply returning `false` for a mismatch.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The global change of token IDs from UUID to 'onrtac:<uuid>'-style strings for every issued jti (TokenManager.initToken, services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/TokenManager.java:1048-1055) has no end-to-end assertion: no test verifies the actual AccessToken.getId()/jti shape from a real flow per grant type (auth code → 'ac', refresh → 'rt', client-credentials transient → 'tr', offline refresh → 'of', exchange → 'te', device → 'dg', ciba → 'ci'); only 4 event expectations were updated, and token exchange, password, UMA, and client-credentials flows have no assertions on their encoded token IDs, so regressions in this de-facto contract consumed by event logs and downstream parsers are invisible to CI.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a nontrivial, cross-cutting change where access token IDs are no longer plain UUIDs: TokenManager.initToken now encodes context into the token id via TokenContextEncoderProvider (services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/TokenManager.java, around initToken). CI coverage added in this diff is limited: there is only a unit test for parsing/encoding (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest) and only 4 event-based expectations were updated in AssertEvents (code-to-token, device, refresh, ciba). The diff shows no analogous end-to-end assertions for other flows mentioned (e.g., token exchange, password, UMA/permission grant, client-credentials), even though those flows set Constants.GRANT_TYPE in various places (e.g., StandardTokenExchangeProvider, ResourceOwnerPasswordCredentialsGrantType, PermissionGrantTypeFactory provides shortcut, etc.). So regressions in the encoded token-id contract for those grants would not be caught by the added/modified tests shown here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: sessionType and tokenType prefixes are never asserted anywhere — nothing verifies transient sessions encode 'tr', lightweight tokens encode 'lt', or offline refresh encodes 'of'.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Copy-paste null-check bug in AccessTokenContext (~66-69): Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed") null-checks grantType twice while rawTokenId is effectively unchecked, so a null rawTokenId would silently produce 'onrtac:null' token IDs in any future caller deviating from KeycloakModelUtils.generateId(); no unit test constructs AccessTokenContext with null arguments, which would have exposed this immediately.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Missing decoder edge-case tests for the IllegalArgumentException branches of getTokenContextFromTokenId (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider ~70-104): encoded-context length ≠ 6 (e.g., 'onrta:1234' or 'onrtacc:1234'), unknown session-type shortcut (e.g., 'xxrtac:1'), unknown token-type shortcut (e.g., 'onxxac:1'), and raw ID containing a colon (indexOf takes the first colon while isAccessTokenId's split(":") assumes exactly one) are untested, leaving the API-facing error semantics unpinned.

adjudication_records.issue_text: getShortcut() was added as a non-default abstract method on OAuth2GrantTypeFactory, breaking all existing custom grant implementations - deployed custom factories that are not recompiled will fail provider instantiation at startup and their grant stops working after upgrade; a default method returning a safe value (e.g. the id or "na") would preserve compatibility

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new non-default abstract method `String getShortcut();` to the `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` interface (server-spi-private). Existing compiled implementations that don’t implement this method will still load, but will throw `AbstractMethodError` when Keycloak calls `gtf.getShortcut()` during startup in `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit()` while iterating `factory.getProviderFactoriesStream(OAuth2GrantType.class)`. adjudication_records.issue_text: Hidden invariant: the decoder hard-requires exactly 2-char shortcuts (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider's encodedContext.length() != 6 check), but the getShortcut() javadoc misleadingly suggests a '3-letters' shortcut and factory postInit validates uniqueness but never length - a custom grant returning a 1- or 3-char shortcut will encode fine but the framework throws IllegalArgumentException when decoding; the length contract must be documented on the interface and enforced at startup

adjudication.rationale: Diff introduces OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut() with javadoc saying "usually like 3-letters shortcut" (OAuth2GrantTypeFactory) but DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider hard-codes decoding to exactly 6 chars of context (2 session + 2 token + 2 grant) and rejects any other length (`if (encodedContext.length() != 6) throw ...`; then `substring(4,6)` for grant). Encoding (`encodeTokenId`) concatenates the grant shortcut without enforcing it is 2 chars, and factory postInit only checks uniqueness, not length. A custom grant returning 1 or 3+ chars would produce token IDs that cannot be decoded and would throw IllegalArgumentException at runtime, so the length contract should be documented/enforced.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Grant-type state is set in five scattered locations (OAuth2GrantTypeBase.java:109, ResourceOwnerPasswordCredentialsGrantType.java:134, PreAuthorizedCodeGrantType.java:82, StandardTokenExchangeProvider.java:237, and TokenManager.java:248's hardcoded OAuth2Constants.REFRESH_TOKEN) with no choke point - forgetting to set Constants.GRANT_TYPE fails silently (token encodes as "na" with no warning), while a typo'd or unregistered value makes encodeTokenId throw IllegalStateException and turns the token endpoint into a 500

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce a new dependency on ClientSessionContext having a correct Constants.GRANT_TYPE attribute for token-id encoding: TokenManager.initToken() now calls TokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId(), which in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId() throws IllegalStateException when the grant type cannot be mapped to a shortcut. At the same time, DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext() silently falls back to UNKNOWN ("na") when the attribute is absent. The finding is also correct that GRANT_TYPE is being set in multiple disparate places in this diff (OAuth2GrantTypeBase, ROPC, pre-authorized code, token exchange, refresh), with no single choke point enforcing presence/validity or logging on fallback. This is mainly a maintainability/robustness concern introduced by the change rather than a proven immediate functional bug for built-in flows (they all appear to set a known grant type).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Duplicate-shortcut validation for the grants SPI lives inside the encoder factory's postInit (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory) - an invariant of OAuth2GrantTypeFactory is enforced by a different SPI's provider factory, so replacing the default encoder provider silently removes validation

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut()` and relies on shortcuts being unique (used in `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId()` / `getTokenContextFromTokenId()`). However, the only explicit duplicate-shortcut detection is in `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit()` via the map-size check and `IllegalStateException`. The uniqueness invariant is not enforced by the grants SPI itself (`OAuth2GrantTypeFactory`) and would not necessarily run if a different `TokenContextEncoderProviderFactory` implementation replaces the default one, so the validation is coupled to the default encoder factory rather than to grant registration.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The lazy-refresh paths in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory (getShortcutByGrantType/getGrantTypeByShortcut, lines ~104-138) insert into the maps without re-running the collision check, so a refresh-time collision silently overwrites grantsByShortcuts and the shortcut decodes to the wrong grant for previously issued tokens; the refresh paths are also speculative complexity since Keycloak does not hot-deploy providers into a running KeycloakSessionFactory

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory, the lazy-refresh branches do mutate the shared maps without any re-validation for shortcut collisions (getShortcutByGrantType: grantsByShortcuts.put(shortcut, grantType); getGrantTypeByShortcut: grantsByShortcuts.put(shortcut, newGrantType)). That means if these refresh paths ever run and a newly discovered/loaded OAuth2GrantTypeFactory reuses an existing shortcut, the mapping could be overwritten and later decoding could resolve the shortcut to a different grant than earlier tokens expected. However, the diff alone does not establish that provider factories can be added after postInit (the code comments speculate about new grants being deployed), so the problematic overwrite scenario is not verifiably reachable from what’s shown; it’s primarily an architecture/robustness concern introduced by the new “refresh maps” complexity.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AccessTokenContext constructor copy-paste bug: the fourth null check re-checks grantType instead of rawTokenId (Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")), so a null rawTokenId passes validation and would later stringify as "onrtcc:null" in the token ID instead of failing fast

The decode path (TokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId, DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId’s parsing/exception semantics + UNKNOWN fallback, and DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory’s shortcut refresh logic) is only exercised by the newly added unit test DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest and has no shown production callers. adjudication_records.issue_text: Layering leak: the encode package now depends on protocol.oidc.mappers, and AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.getShouldUseLightweightToken was widened to public static solely so the encoder can call it - lightweight-token policy belongs in a neutral OIDC config utility, and the new mappers-encode dependency widens API surface and will make future refactoring awkward

To enable this, `AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.getShouldUseLightweightToken` was changed from package-private instance method to `public static` (widened API surface) specifically to be callable from the new encoder code.
