adjudication_records.issue_text: Constants.GRANT_TYPE is a pure alias of OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE - two public constants with the same name and value in sibling classes is a standing invitation to use the wrong one and creates future divergence confusion; referencing OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE at the use sites would suffice

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds `public static final String GRANT_TYPE = OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE;` in `org.keycloak.models.Constants`, making it a direct alias of `org.keycloak.OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE`. This creates two public constants with the same semantic meaning/value in different classes, which can cause API/confusion/maintenance divergence risk (e.g., callers may inconsistently import/use one vs the other). It’s not a correctness defect by itself, but it is a real, diff-grounded design concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: OAuth2GrantType.Context.grantType snapshots unvalidated client input at construction time (formParams.getFirst(OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE)) instead of deriving it from the provider's own factory ID - it can be null if form params lack the key and goes stale if the public setFormParams is later used to swap parameters; the authoritative value should be the factory ID the endpoint dispatched on

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show `OAuth2GrantType.Context` now capturing `grantType` once in the constructor via `formParams.getFirst(OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE)` and exposing `setFormParams(...)` without updating `grantType`, so the stored value can become stale if `setFormParams` is used later. It can also be null if the form param is missing. This value is then propagated into `ClientSessionContext` (`clientSessionCtx.setAttribute(Constants.GRANT_TYPE, context.getGrantType())`) and used by the new token-id encoding path. However, the diff alone doesn’t prove this causes broken behavior in practice (token endpoint likely requires `grant_type`, and dispatch probably already aligns with it), so it’s more of an architectural/correctness concern than a clearly verifiable defect from the patch alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unit test passes for the wrong reason: DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest's before() calls init(null) but never postInit so sessionFactory is null, and in testIncorrectGrantType the refresh path throws an NPE that is swallowed by the broad catch (RuntimeException) - the test never exercises the IllegalArgumentException branch it claims to verify; the test also seeds package-private mutable factory fields (factory.grantsByShortcuts) directly, coupling it to factory internals

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest.before(), the factory calls init(null) but never postInit(), leaving DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.sessionFactory unset. In testIncorrectGrantType(), parsing tokenId "ofrtac:5678" leads to DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId() calling factory.getGrantTypeByShortcut("ac"). Because "ac" is not present in the test-seeded grantsByShortcuts map, getGrantTypeByShortcut() takes the refresh path and dereferences sessionFactory (null), causing an NPE. That NPE is swallowed by the broad catch (RuntimeException), so the test passes without exercising the provider’s intended IllegalArgumentException branch for unknown grant shortcuts. Also, the test directly mutates factory.grantsByShortcuts/grantsToShortcuts (package-private fields), tightly coupling the test to factory internals.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Likely-unused import TokenExchangeGrantTypeFactory added in StandardTokenExchangeProvider.java:50 - the added line uses OAuth2Constants.TOKEN_EXCHANGE_GRANT_TYPE directly and there is no GRANT_TYPE constant on that factory; leftover from an abandoned approach

The added logic uses `OAuth2Constants.TOKEN_EXCHANGE_GRANT_TYPE` directly (`clientSessionCtx.setAttribute(Constants.GRANT_TYPE, OAuth2Constants.TOKEN_EXCHANGE_GRANT_TYPE);`), and no `TokenExchangeGrantTypeFactory` symbol appears elsewhere in that file in the diff. This is therefore a verifiable unused-import cleanup issue (potentially CI/style-check failing depending on project rules), not a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Public OAuth2GrantType.Context(Context) copy constructor was removed - external grant implementations that construct derived contexts this way will no longer compile; a deprecated forwarding constructor would have been safer if removal was necessary

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the `public Context(Context context)` copy constructor from `OAuth2GrantType.Context` (see `OAuth2GrantType.java`, where the entire forwarding constructor block is deleted). Since `server-spi-private` types are part of the SPI surface used by grant implementations, any existing/custom `OAuth2GrantType` implementations that relied on `new Context(existingContext)` will no longer compile. This is a backward-compatibility/API stability concern rather than a runtime correctness defect shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The token-ID wire format is a persisted, cross-version contract but is implemented as a swappable per-deployment SPI (TokenContextEncoderSpi) with no feature flag, migration note, or documentation that the format must remain stable - swapping the TokenContextEncoderProvider orphans every previously issued token ID and a custom provider has no stated compatibility obligation; the format should be treated as a versioned contract

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes access token `jti` generation from a plain UUID to an encoded format produced by a provider SPI: `TokenManager.initToken` now does `session.getProvider(TokenContextEncoderProvider.class)` and `token.id(encoder.encodeTokenId(tokenCtx))`. A new internal SPI (`TokenContextEncoderSpi`) and default factory are added, but nothing in the diff constrains deployments from supplying a different `TokenContextEncoderProvider` with a different encoding/decoding scheme. Since token IDs are emitted externally (at least via events; tests were updated from `isUUID()` to `isAccessTokenId(...)`), making the wire format depend on a swappable provider is an architectural/compatibility concern grounded in this change, even if it may not be an immediate correctness defect in the default configuration.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AssertEvents.java:483 (isAccessTokenId matcher): inverted logic — the matcher returns false (mismatch) when the grant shortcut equals the expected value and falls through to pass when it doesn't, so a correct token would fail the assertion while a wrong-grant token passes as long as the tail is a UUID

adjudication.rationale: In AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId matcher (new code around line ~483), matchesSafely does `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`, which explicitly fails when the extracted grant shortcut equals the expected value, and otherwise falls through to return `isUUID().matches(items[1])`. This inverts the intended logic described in the finding: a correct-grant token would be rejected while an incorrect-grant token could pass as long as the raw id portion is a UUID. (Additionally, the substring indices appear inconsistent with the comment/format, but the inversion alone is a verifiable correctness defect.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: AssertEvents.java:483 (isAccessTokenId matcher): wrong substring index — the grant shortcut occupies chars 4–5 so substring(4, 6) is required, not substring(3, 5), which reads the last char of the token type plus the first char of the grant type (e.g. 'ta' for 'onrtac') and throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException on short prefixes; fixing only the inversion without the index would make every legitimate token fail, and combined the guard can never reject anything, so the four updated assertions (expectCodeToToken, expectDeviceCodeToToken, expectRefresh, expectAuthReqIdToToken) verify nothing about grant encoding and the PR's only end-to-end integration check goes green even if the encoding is entirely wrong

adjudication.rationale: In AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId, the grant shortcut in the encoded token prefix is the last 2 chars of the 6-char context (sessionType[0..1] + tokenType[2..3] + grant[4..5]), so it should be extracted with substring(4, 6). The added code uses substring(3, 5), which reads 1 char from tokenType plus 1 from grant (e.g., "tc" for prefix "trltcc"). Additionally, the condition is inverted: `if (..equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` rejects the expected value. Combined, this matcher will usually never validate the grant portion and will often pass as long as the suffix is a UUID, making the updated event assertions effectively not check grant encoding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:74 (decoder) vs :110–118 (encoder) and OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.java:29–33 (contract): the decoder hard-requires the context prefix to be exactly 6 chars (i.e. 2-char shortcuts) while the encoder blindly concatenates getShortcut() output with no length check and postInit performs no format validation, and the getShortcut() javadoc explicitly invites 3-letter shortcuts — a custom grant returning e.g. 'abc' mints tokens that encodeTokenId accepts but whose getTokenContextFromTokenId always throws IllegalArgumentException (mint path green, decode path red, no startup-time detection)

adjudication.rationale: Verified in diff: DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId() requires the prefix before ':' to be exactly 6 chars (2 for sessionType + 2 for tokenType + 2 for grantType) and throws IllegalArgumentException otherwise. But encodeTokenId() concatenates sessionType(2) + tokenType(2) + grantShort with no length check, and DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit() stores whatever OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut() returns with no format validation. Additionally, OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut() javadoc says shortcuts are “usually like 3-letters”, which would produce a 7-char prefix and therefore decode would always fail for such a custom grant (mint path succeeds, decode path throws), with no startup-time detection.

adjudication_records.issue_text: DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:76: a grant factory whose getShortcut() returns null NPEs in ConcurrentHashMap.put during postInit, causing whole-server boot failure with a confusing NPE because there is no null check on shortcuts

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit, the code unconditionally does `String grantShortcut = gtf.getShortcut(); grantsByShortcuts.put(grantShortcut, grantName);` where `grantsByShortcuts` is a `ConcurrentHashMap`. `ConcurrentHashMap` rejects null keys/values and will throw an NPE if any `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` implementation returns `null` from `getShortcut()`. The diff adds `getShortcut()` to the SPI but does not enforce non-null/validate with a clearer error, so a misbehaving/third-party grant factory could cause a confusing boot-time NPE. However, the diff itself updates the shown built-in factories to return non-null shortcuts, and we can’t verify any existing factory returns null from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: A grant shortcut containing ':' silently corrupts the raw-id split in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId, the split is done on the first ':' (indexOf), and then the code validates the prefix length must be exactly 6, otherwise it throws IllegalArgumentException. So a grant shortcut containing ':' would not “silently corrupt” the raw-id split; it would result in an exception due to the encodedContext length check. Also, all shortcuts added in this diff are fixed 2-letter strings without ':'.

adjudication_records.issue_text: OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.java:31: the new abstract getShortcut() method was added to the factory SPI with no default implementation, so pre-compiled third-party grant extensions (a known custom-grant extension point) throw AbstractMethodError when postInit iterates all factories calling gtf.getShortcut(), preventing the entire Keycloak server from starting after the upgrade

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new abstract method `String getShortcut()` to the `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` SPI (server-spi-private) with no default implementation. Existing precompiled third-party implementations of this interface would not have the method, causing binary incompatibility. The new code in `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit(...)` unconditionally casts each `OAuth2GrantType` provider factory to `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` and calls `gtf.getShortcut()`, which would trigger an `AbstractMethodError` at runtime for older extensions and could prevent server startup.

adjudication_records.issue_text: OAuth2GrantType: the public Context(Context) copy constructor was removed, a source break for any extension code using it

adjudication.rationale: In OAuth2GrantType.Context, the diff removes the previously existing public copy constructor `public Context(Context context)` (see the deleted block in `server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantType.java`).
